title: Assessment Administration Coordinator
description:
Assessment Administration Coordinator

Location: Nominal office of York, with expected minimum attendance of once per month
Salary: £27,010 gross per annum
Contract: Full Time, Permanent

Applications close on 14th September at 9am. Interviews will take place via MS Teams w/c 28th September

Benefits:
- A generous pension plan with USS
- Enhanced family leave benefits
- 31 days annual leave, plus bank holidays
- Flexible working hours
- Hybrid work
- Employee Assistance Programme access
- Personal Financial Wellbeing advice access

to name a few

The Role:

We are looking for an Assessment Administration Coordinator to support the delivery of a range of prestigious peer review and assessment services across the higher education sector.

This role will provide end-to-end administrative support for either institutional services (including Athena Swan, Race Equality Charter, Inclusive Institutions Framework, Impact Awards and Accreditation) or individual services (including Fellowship, End-Point Assessment and Awards).

You will play a vital role in ensuring assessment processes run smoothly, efficiently and accurately, supporting applicants, reviewers, institutions and subject experts throughout the assessment journey.

Working within a collaborative team, you will help deliver excellent customer experiences while contributing to ongoing service improvements and transformation projects.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys coordinating multiple priorities and has a strong commitment to quality, accuracy and continuous improvement.

There are 3 opportunities available for this role, 1 permanent position within Institutional Services and 2 Fixed Term Contracts within Individual Services.

Job requirements
- Experience delivering high-quality administrative support within education or a related professional environment.
- Proven experience delivering excellent customer service and handling customer enquiries and complaints.
- Experience working with databases, CRM systems and case management systems.
- Experience using multiple digital systems to record, manage and monitor data accurately.
- Experience supporting external customers and stakeholders at varying levels of seniority.
- Knowledge and experience of Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word and PowerPoint.
- Experience managing confidential and sensitive information appropriately.

Job responsibilities

Assessment Process Administration
- Support the effective administration of end-to-end peer review assessment processes across both institutional and individual services.
- Conduct initial quality assurance checks on applications to ensure eligibility requirements and submission standards are met prior to review.
- Coordinate assessment activities and ensure results are released accurately and within published timescales.
- Provide administrative support for assessment panels, peer review meetings and reviewer activities.
- Prepare, issue and manage assessment outcomes, feedback documentation and certification for successful applicants.
- Maintain accurate records and data throughout the assessment lifecycle in accordance with compliance requirements and service standards.
- Support the administration of peer reviewers, consultants and other associates involved in assessment delivery.

Customer Service and Stakeholder Support
- Respond to application and post-recognition enquiries in a timely, professional and customer-focused manner.
- Escalate complex issues appropriately while maintaining a positive customer experience.
- Build strong working relationships with institutional contacts, contract holders, programme leaders, programme administrators and subject expert teams.
- Support a seamless customer and member experience across all assessment services.
- Maintain up-to-date knowledge of products, services, systems and processes to provide accurate guidance and support.

Data Management and Reporting
- Maintain and monitor information within databases, CRM systems and assessment platforms.
- Produce reports and administrative data to support operational monitoring and service delivery.
- Support annual HESA and international data returns where applicable.
- Ensure all records are accurate, secure and compliant with GDPR and organisational policies.

Continuous Improvement and Transformation
- Contribute ideas to improve administrative efficiency and enhance customer experiences.
- Support assessment delivery transformation projects, including system testing, piloting and process improvements.
- Actively contribute to a culture of continuous improvement and innovation.
- Keep process documentation up to date and support the implementation of new systems and ways of working.

Compliance and Governance
- Ensure policies, procedures and regulatory requirements are consistently followed.
- Uphold organisational commitments relating to equality, diversity and inclusion, data protection, health and safety and charity governance.
- Handle sensitive and confidential information with professionalism and discretion.

What you'll get

You'll have the opportunity to shape how finance supports the organisation, influence decision-making at all levels, and lead a team committed to delivering an excellent service. In return, you'll join a collaborative and values-driven organisation where your expertise, leadership and ideas will make a real difference.

If you're an experienced finance professional who combines strong operational leadership with a passion for developing people and improving processes, we'd love to hear from you.

Advance HE is a member-led, sector-owned charity that works with institutions and higher education across the world to improve higher education for staff, students and society.

Our strategic priorities of: maximising membership impact and value, supporting leadership, management and governance development for transformational change and developing educational excellence for the higher education of the future supports the work of our members and the sector.

It is our people and the people we help that really make us who we are!

To apply:

If you have the skills and experience required for this role, please click on Apply today to be taken to our site to complete your application.

Advance HE is committed to providing equal opportunities for everyone regardless of their background.

No agencies please.

title: Office Administrator
description:
Are you a proactive and confident Office Administrator who enjoys working in a busy, sociable environment where no two days are quite the same?

Would you like to join a growing financial services business in Pickering, where you ll be trusted to manage your own workload, build relationships with clients and develop your knowledge along the way?

We are looking for an organised and personable Office Administrator to join our client s friendly, open-plan office.

This is a permanent opportunity offering plenty of variety. You ll be working with different systems, communicating regularly with clients and supporting the team with the administration needed to keep client records accurate, compliant and up to date.

You don t need to know everything about the industry day one. What s important is that you re proactive, confident communicating with people and comfortable taking ownership of your work. You ll receive training and development to build your understanding of the legislation and compliance and reporting as your job evolves.

The office is busy, chatty and collaborative, with a relaxed dress code and it s dog friendly too!

What the Office Administrator job involves

You ll provide day-to-day administrative support to the team while helping to ensure clients receive an efficient and professional service.
- Completing and processing client forms and documentation.
- Contacting clients to chase outstanding information, documents and signatures.
- Ensuring the required documentation is received and recorded for compliance purposes.
- Keeping client information and records accurate and up to date.
- Using a number of different systems to manage information and administrative processes.
- Creating reports and letters from templates to send to clients.
- Communicating confidently with clients by telephone and email.

This role would suit someone who enjoys taking responsibility for their work rather than waiting to be given their next task.

Skills required

We re looking for someone who is organised, approachable and comfortable working in a busy environment. You ll ideally have:
- Previous administration experience is essential.
- Strong organisational skills and excellent attention to detail.
- A proactive approach and the confidence to use your own initiative.
- Good written and verbal communication skills.
- Confidence speaking with people over the phone.
- The ability to self-manage and prioritise a varied workload.
- Good IT skills and the ability to learn and work across several different systems.
- A professional approach when handling confidential information.

Other information
- Full time working 8:30am 5:00pm Monday to Thursday and 8:30am 1:30pm Friday
- 20 days annual leave plus bank holidays.
- Your birthday off.
- Lunch provided each day.
- Access to free financial advice.
- Performance-related end-of-year bonus.
- Training and development including paid for professional qualifications.
- A friendly, open-plan and dog-friendly working environment.

This vacancy is being advertised through KD Recruitment Limited who are operating as an Employment Agency.

Due to the volume of applications we receive if you have not heard from us within 2 weeks, please assume you have not been short listed for this particular role.

KD Recruitment Limited is committed to a policy of equal opportunities in relation to job applications and we are also committed to protecting your personal data. If you would like to read our privacy policy, please go to our website where you will find all the information you need to know about how we will use and process your personal data.

You can also follow us on Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, and LinkedIn for up to date jobs and other helpful information.

title: Office Administrator
description:
Job Title: Office Administrator

Salary: £28,000 - £30,000 per annum, dependent on experience

Location: Masham, North Yorkshire (HG4 4 JB)

Job Type: Full Time, Permanent

Join a Successful Family Business with a Proud Heritage

For over 126 years, I'Anson Bros Ltd has been at the forefront of animal feed manufacturing, growing from our Yorkshire roots into one of the UK's leading feed producers. As a fifth-generation family-owned business, we combine traditional values with a progressive approach, serving customers locally, nationally, and internationally from our sites in Masham and Dalton, Thirsk.

As we continue to grow, we're looking for a friendly, organised, and proactive Office Administrator to become an important part of our Masham team.

About the role:

This is a varied and rewarding role at the heart of our business. You'll be the first point of contact for many of our customers and suppliers, helping to ensure the smooth day-to-day running of the office while delivering excellent service.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Handling incoming customer calls and enquiries
- Processing invoices and administrative paperwork
- Supporting colleagues across various departments
- Maintaining accurate records and documentation
- Assisting with general office administration duties

About You:

We're looking for someone who enjoys working with people, takes pride in being organised, and thrives in a busy office environment.

You'll ideally have:
- A positive, friendly, and professional manner
- Excellent communication and customer service skills
- A proactive approach to problem-solving
- The ability to prioritise tasks and work efficiently within a team
- Strong organisational and administrative skills
- Experience in office administration

Knowledge of agriculture, farming, or the wider rural community would be advantageous but isn't essential.

Why Join I'Anson Bros?

We believe our people are key to our success, which is why we offer a supportive environment where you can develop and grow your career.

Our benefits include:
- 22 days annual leave, increasing with length of service, plus bank holidays
- Company pension scheme
- Fuel allowance to help with travel costs
- Comprehensive in-house training
- Career development and progression opportunities
- Death in service benefit

A welcoming, supportive team culture within a successful family business

Ready to Join Us?

If you're looking for a rewarding role within a well-established Yorkshire business that values its people and invests in their future, we'd love to hear from you. Join us and play a part in the next chapter of the I'Anson Bros story.

Please click the APPLY button to send your CV and Cover Letter for this role.

Candidates with experience of; Office Administrator, Administrator, Office Administration Assistant, Administration Clerk, Administrative Assistant, Office Coordinator, Receptionist, Secretary, Business Administrator, Support Administrator, Reception Administrator, Office Assistant, Office Coordinator, Office Manager, Business Administrator may also be considered for this role.

description: An opportunity has arisen for a fixed term 6 month position to work in the reception of Hummingbird house, home to the Harrogate & Ripon Community Treatment team. Hummingbird House accommodates Adult Mental Health teams and CAMHS, the opportunity is within the adult reception team. Hummingbird House is situated in the centre of Harrogate Town, a short walk from local shops and amenities, as well as being located close to the central bus terminal and train station. As a member of our Hummingbird House reception team you will be the first point of contact for patients, families, and visitors, you will play a vital role in creating a welcoming and supportive environment at the heart of the hospital. This is an opportunity to make a real difference by proving both practical assistance and a kind reassuring presence. The role will involve managing incoming and outgoing post, room bookings, ordering supplies, logging calls with estates, dealing with prescriptions, petty cash, booking taxis or patient transport, arranging collection of pathology samples, and general office duties. The ability to remain calm, communicate clearly, adhere to confidentiality, and promote a positive culture for those living with mental health issues and/or learning disabilities. The successful candidate will be expected to perform basic admin tasks, update clinic lists, maintain visitor logs, issue access cards, deal with incoming & outgoing post, photocopying and ensure that all information in the reception area for staff and the public is clearly displayed and updated as appropriate. If successful you will be supplied with a job plan and a fully supported induction. description: A rare opportunity has arisen for a dedicated and experienced administrator to join our friendly team based at Alexander House. Our team provides essential compassionate mental health support and care to our older people in the local area and is situated in the beautiful and historical market town of Knaresborough. Alexander House is just a short 10-minute walk to local amenities and has free onsite parking. As an essential part of the community/memory team, you will be based in the admin office and be supported by our existing welcoming administrators to work closely with the clinical staff in delivering our Trust mission of co-creating a great experience for our patients, carers, and families. If you are an individual with experience working in a busy office environment, who is confident in using IT systems including Outlook for effective diary management. Someone who thrives in a dynamic busy setting and is keen to join a team striving to make a real difference in your local community then we are looking for you. You must have the Right to Work in the UK in order to be successfully appointed to this role. Please note, this role does not meet the required eligibility criteria for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker visa and therefore the Trust is unable to offer sponsorship for this particular role. Whilst having previous experience in an administrative role is essential, NHS or other health care experience is not. We are first and foremost looking for a colleague with a passion for helping people who believes in delivering excellent customer service, who has a keen interest in learning and working in a health care setting with a 'can do' attitude. This role is at the heart of the multi-disciplinary team which means you will work closely with nurses, healthcare professionals, consultants, and management to ensure that they have everything admin wise they need to provide the best possible care to our patients. We are looking for someone who is comfortable multitasking, someone who can communicate confidently, build strong working relationships with a variety of people, who can prioritise their workload and who is genuinely interested in understanding and supporting the challenges that mental health care provides. Your main duties will be processing referrals to the team, booking assessment and treatment appointments, liaising with patients, carers and other stakeholders, typing letters and maintaining accurate, confidential patient records. For more details, please read carefully the job description, to be successful at shortlisting please briefly describe how you match this description citing examples to reinforce your experience. If you do not have maths or English to the required standard please state your intention to work towards. Our Trust is dedicated to supporting our colleagues in providing an excellent working environment and encourages everyone to share their progressive ideas. All staff have regular 1-2-1 supervisions and an annual appraisal, which provides lots of opportunity for celebration of achievements, and discussions around challenges, and your aspirations. You will work alongside other team administrators and our senior administrators (medical secretaries) to deliver admin support. As a valuable member of the team, you will be invited to attend regular meetings to improve your knowledge and understanding of the services, you will also be required to minute meetings and keep accurate records. If successful, you will be supplied with a job plan and a fully supported induction.
